And he wrote a small document and gave it to her, that she should stand where the Caliph was passing,
and cry out as though she were wronged,
and hold out the document.
And when they took it from her,
she should not stay any longer,
lest she be found.
Now, in the document he wrote as follows:
"By God, who exalted the horn of the Christians through Jesus son of Nestorius,
and of the Jews through Manasseh son of al-Qazzaz the fuller {OCR?},
and brought low the Muslims through you (him):
I adjure you to look into my wrong."
When she did this,
and al-Aziz read these words,
and understood their meaning,
they searched for the woman,
and she was not found.
And he was enraged,
and imprisoned Jesus and Manasseh.
And because Jesus was beloved by all the courtiers,
the daughter of King al-Aziz requested him from her father,
and he gave three hundred thousand dinars to the king,
and restored him again to his office.
And at that time,
when the people of Tagrit were afflicted by the exactions of oppressive rulers,
they went forth from their city,
and were scattered among the regions.
And wherever they came, they built churches and monasteries,
and adorned temples.
Among them were these three honorable brothers,
who were called the sons of Abu Imran,
and they came and lived in Melitene.
And they built churches in it,
and convents for women,
and outside of it, monasteries for monks.
And on every Friday,
they distributed alms to the poor from morning until noon.
And the Emperor of the Romans envied them,
and compelled them to mint the imperial darics for one year.
And they did so,
and their wealth was not diminished.
And even Emperor Basil himself was in need, and came to their door,
and asked a loan from them.
And when they saw him,
they fell down and worshipped him,
and gave him a hundred centenaria of gold.
And afterwards he repaid them,
because he was just.
And at another time,
when the Turks raided the territory of Melitene,
again that old man Abu Salim, the elder brother, happened to come from the monastery,
and was taken in captivity.
And when the Turks said to him:
"Ransom yourself,
because you are rich,"
he replied:
"If you will sell all the captives,
I will buy them."
And the Turks laughed and said to him:
"How much will you give?" And he said:
"For each person, five dinars."
